Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import AbstractSyntax Deref HeapUpdate.

Reserved Notation "t1 ↦ t2" (at level 40, t2 at level 39).

Inductive red : config -> config -> Prop :=

| red_read : forall yObj wObj m Sigma e Lv yVal wVal ds fs,
    fresh_in_config (wVal :: nil) (trm_read (avar_f wObj) m; fs ; Sigma; e; Lv) ->
    binds wObj yObj e ->
    binds yObj (item_obj ds) Sigma ->
    defs_has ds (def_fld m (avar_f yVal)) ->
    (trm_read (avar_f wObj) m; fs ; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (trm_var (avar_f wVal); fs; Sigma; e & wVal ~ yVal; fv_config (trm_read (avar_f wObj) m; fs ; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_write : forall yObj wObj m Sigma e Lv yArg wArg Sigma' fs,
    heap_update Sigma yObj m yArg Sigma' ->
    binds wObj yObj e ->
    binds wArg yArg e ->
    (trm_write (avar_f wObj) m (avar_f wArg); fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (trm_var (avar_f wArg); fs ; Sigma'; e; fv_config (trm_write (avar_f wObj) m (avar_f wArg); fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_call : forall yObj wObj m Sigma e Lv wArg t ds fs,
    binds yObj (item_obj ds) Sigma ->
    defs_has ds (def_met m t) ->
    binds wObj yObj e ->
    (trm_call (avar_f wObj) m (avar_f wArg); fs ; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ ((open wArg (open_rec 1 wObj t)); fs ; Sigma; e; fv_config (trm_call (avar_f wObj) m (avar_f wArg); fs ; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_apply : forall yFun wFun wArg Sigma e Lv t fs,
    binds yFun (item_fun t) Sigma ->
    binds wFun yFun e ->
    (trm_apply (avar_f wFun) (avar_f wArg); fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (open wArg t; fs; Sigma; e; fv_config (trm_apply (avar_f wFun) (avar_f wArg); fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_let_fun : forall T t1 t2 Sigma e Lv y w fs,
    fresh_in_config (y :: w :: nil) (trm_lit (lit_fun T t1) t2 ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv) ->
    y <> w ->
    (trm_lit (lit_fun T t1) t2 ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (open w t2 ; fs; Sigma & y ~ (item_fun t1); e & w ~ y ; fv_config (trm_lit (lit_fun T t1) t2 ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_let_obj : forall T ds t Sigma e Lv y w fs,
    fresh_in_config (y :: w :: nil) (trm_lit (lit_obj T ds) t ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv) ->
    w <> y ->
    (trm_lit (lit_obj T ds) t ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (open w t ; fs; Sigma & y ~ (item_obj (deref_defs (e & w ~ y) (open w ds))); e & w ~ y ; fv_config (trm_lit (lit_obj T ds) t ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_let_var : forall t Sigma e Lv x fs,
    (trm_var (avar_f x); (stack_cons (frame_let t) fs); Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (open x t; fs; Sigma; e ; fv_config (trm_var (avar_f x); (stack_cons (frame_let t) fs); Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_let_push : forall s t fs Sigma e Lv,
    (trm_let s t; fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (s; (stack_cons (frame_let t) fs); Sigma; e ; fv_config (trm_let s t; fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

where "t1 ↦ t2" := (red t1 t2).

Inductive answer: config -> Prop :=
| nf_loc: forall x Sigma e Lv, answer (trm_var (avar_f x); stack_nil; Sigma; e; Lv).

Reserved Notation "C1 ⊣ n ↦* C2"
         (at level 40, n at level 41, C2 at level 39).

Inductive red_closure :  config -> nat -> config -> Prop :=

| red_refl : forall (C : config),
    C ⊣ 0 ↦* C

| red_trans : forall (C1 C2 C3 : config) (n : nat),
    C1 ⊣ n ↦* C2 ->
    C2      ↦  C3 ->
    C1 ⊣ S n ↦* C3

where "C1 ⊣ n ↦* C2" := (red_closure C1 n C2).

Definition config_terminates_in C n :=
 (exists (Ca : config), answer Ca /\ (C ⊣n↦* Ca)).

Definition config_terminates C :=
 (exists (n : nat), config_terminates_in C n).

Lemma imm_binds_in_dom A (S : env A) x v : @binds A x v S -> x \in dom S.

(* A freshly allocated location is not a member of the domain. *)
Lemma imm_fresh_head_notin_dom (S : heap) (t : trm) (st : stack)
      (e : renv) (Lv : fset var) (y w : var) :
  fresh_in_config (y :: w :: nil) (config_mk t st S e Lv) ->
  y \notin dom S.
Proof.
  intros Hf.
  unfold fresh_in_config in Hf.
  cbn [LibList.length] in Hf.
  destruct Hf as [Hy _].
  apply notin_union_r in Hy; destruct Hy as [_ Hy].
  apply notin_union_r in Hy; destruct Hy as [_ Hy].
  apply notin_union_r in Hy; destruct Hy as [Hy _].
  apply notin_union_r in Hy; tauto.

      (st : stack) (e : renv) (Lv : fset var) (y w : var) :

  fresh_in_config (y :: w :: nil) (config_mk t st S e Lv) ->
  z <> y.
Proof.
  intros Hb Hf E. subst z.
  apply (imm_fresh_head_notin_dom Hf).
  eapply imm_binds_in_dom. eassumption.
Qed.

(* A heap update preserves every binding whose key is not the updated one. *)
Lemma imm_binds_heap_update_neq (S S' : heap) (x a : var) (l : fld_label)
      (y : var) (it : item) :
  heap_update S x l a S' -> y <> x -> binds y it S -> binds y it S'.

  unfold heap_update in Hu.
  destruct Hu as (_ & _ & _ & Hpres & _).
  eapply Hpres; eauto.

Proof.
  intros G x T H. induction H; cbn [ctx_dom].
  - rewrite in_union, in_singleton. auto.

(* The whole reduction argument, reduced to the write-target reachability
   property (the soundness/metatheory obligation). *)
Lemma immutability_aux (F : ctx) (T : typ) (C1 : config) :
  ty_config F C1 T ->
  (forall (C2 : config) (n : nat) (yObj wObj : var) (m : fld_label)
          (yArg : var) (fs : stack) (Sigma : heap) (e : renv)
          (Lv : fset var) (ds1 : defs),
      red_closure C1 n C2 ->
      C2 = config_mk (trm_write (avar_f wObj) m (avar_f yArg)) fs Sigma e Lv ->
      binds wObj yObj e ->
      binds yObj (item_obj ds1) (config_heap C1) ->
      F ⊢ C1 mreach yObj) ->
  forall n C2, C1 ⊣ n ↦* C2 ->
    forall y ds, binds y (item_obj ds) (config_heap C1) ->
      binds y (item_obj ds) (config_heap C2) \/ F ⊢ C1 mreach y.
Proof.
  intros Hty Hwrite n C2 Hred.
  induction Hred as [C | C1' C2' C3' n' Hred' IH Hstep].
  - intros y ds Hb. left. exact Hb.
  - intros y ds Hb.
    destruct (IH Hty Hwrite y ds Hb) as [Hpres | Hmr]; [| right; assumption].
    destruct Hstep as
      [ yObj0 wObj0 m0 Sigma0 e0 Lv0 yVal0 wVal0 ds0 fs0 Hfresh Hbw0 Hby0 Hdf0
      | yObj0 wObj0 m0 Sigma0 e0 Lv0 yArg0 wArg0 Sigma0' fs0 Hu0 Hbw0 Hby0
      | yObj0 wObj0 m0 Sigma0 e0 Lv0 wArg0 t0 ds0 fs0 Hby0 Hdf0 Hbw0
      | yFun0 wFun0 wArg0 Sigma0 e0 Lv0 t0 fs0 Hby0 Hbw0
      | T0 t10 t20 Sigma0 e0 Lv0 y0 w0 fs0 Hfresh0 Hneq0
      | T0 ds0 t0 Sigma0 e0 Lv0 y0 w0 fs0 Hfresh0 Hneq0
      | t0 Sigma0 e0 Lv0 x0 fs0
      | s0 t0 fs0 Sigma0 e0 Lv0 ].
    + left. exact Hpres.
    + destruct (classic (y = yObj0)) as [-> | Hneq].
      * right.
        eapply Hwrite; eauto.
      * left. eapply imm_binds_heap_update_neq; eauto.
    + left. exact Hpres.
    + left. exact Hpres.
    + left. eapply binds_push_neq; [ exact Hpres | ].
      eapply imm_binds_fresh_head_neq; eauto.
    + left. eapply binds_push_neq; [ exact Hpres | ].
      eapply imm_binds_fresh_head_neq; eauto.
    + left. exact Hpres.
    + left. exact Hpres.
Qed.

(* Subset transitivity, and monotonicity of the heap domain along reduction. *)
Lemma imm_subset_trans A (E F G : fset A) : E \c F -> F \c G -> E \c G.
Proof. intros H1 H2 x Hx. apply H2, H1, Hx. Qed.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses Program.Equality.

Require Import AbstractSyntax Equivalence RecordTypes TypingMode InertContext Indep GeneralTyping.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

Notation typ_refcap_corr Tw Ty := (
  match (mode_refcap_corr' typing_mode) with
  | mode_refcap_corr_same =>

    Ty = Tw
  | mode_refcap_corr_ref_mutability =>

    exists Tbnd, (Tw = (typ_mut_marker Tbnd) /\ Ty = (typ_mut_marker typ_bot))
  end) (only parsing).

Inductive typ_corr: typ -> typ -> Prop :=
| typ_corr_obj(T S U: typ):
  typ_refcap_corr S U ->
  typ_corr (typ_objref T S) (typ_objref T U)
| typ_corr_fun(t1 t2: typ):
  mode_has_fun typing_mode ->
  typ_corr (typ_fun t1 t2) (typ_fun t1 t2)
.

Inductive renv_corr: ctx -> renv -> Prop :=

| renv_corr_empty(G: ctx):
    renv_corr G renv_empty

| renv_corr_ref(G1 G2 G3: ctx)(e: renv)(w y: var)(Tw Ty: typ):
    ctx_binds_k_after w v_ref Tw G1 G2 ->
    ctx_binds_k_after y v_loc Ty G2 G3 ->
    typ_corr Tw Ty ->
    renv_corr G1 e ->
    renv_corr G1 (renv_bind e w y)
.

End WithTypingMode.

Arguments renv_corr {typing_mode}.

Arguments typ_corr {typing_mode}.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

End WithTypingMode.

Notation env_binds_more e e' :=
  (forall y w, binds w y e -> binds w y e') (only parsing).

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

End WithTypingMode.

Interesting! renv_corr has a peculiar recursive structure: `renv_corr G1 e` and binds w with ctx_binds_k_after w v_ref Tw G1 G2 and y with ctx_binds_k_after y v_loc Ty G2 G3, typ_corr Tw Ty. So a ref var's type Tw relates to the location's type Ty: for mode_refcap_corr_ref_mutability, Tw = typ_mut_marker Tbnd and Ty = typ_mut_marker typ_bot. Hmm wait, typ_corr is between typ_objref T S and typ_objref T U: so Tw and Ty are object reference types. `typ_corr (typ_objref T S) (typ_objref T U)` with typ_refcap_corr S U. In mode_refcap_corr_ref_mutability: exists Tbnd, S = typ_mut_marker Tbnd /\ U = typ_mut_marker typ_bot. So the ref var w has type objref T (marker Tbnd) matching the location y's type objref T (marker bot). So if a ref variable is typed, its receiver type's mutability capability (marker) is matched by the location's mutability marker bot. That's the "truncation" correlation.

Wait, but mreach_trm requires `F ⁏ e ⊢ trm_var (avar_f w) ∶ (typ_mut_marker typ_bot)`. That's typing a bare mut marker, not an objref. Hmm, `typ_mut_marker typ_bot` typing of a variable: ty_var looks up the var's type in ctx. A variable has type typ_mut_marker typ_bot only if bound with exactly that type. In the initial heap, variables of kind v_loc might have type objref, not mut marker. Hmm, but mreach_trm's conclusion is `F ⊢ C1 mreach y` where y is the *location* bound by w. For that, w's type must be `typ_mut_marker typ_bot`. When would a ref variable have type exactly mut marker bot? Maybe for "self" references in objects: field values with mutable marker? Or maybe typ_objref with S = marker bot yields... hmm, typ_and (typ_bnd T) (marker bot). Not equal to marker.

Hmm wait, maybe mreach_trm's w types an object *type* that is mut_marker bot: internal self-variable of an object whose type is a mut marker? In roDOT, `typ_mut_marker T` is a "mutability marker" for the type of "this" inside a mutable object. Hmm.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Inductive mode :=
  | basic
  | basic_no_fun
  | basic_incap
  | basic_sef_typing
  | rodot
  | rodot_top_nm
  | rodot_nm_compl
  | rodot_nm_muttop
  | rodot_nm_compl_muttop
  | rodot_sef.

Class Mode := mode_m: mode.

Definition mode_has_fun' m: bool := match m with
| basic | basic_sef_typing => true
| _ => false
end.

Notation mode_has_fun m := ((mode_has_fun' m) = true)(only parsing).

Definition mode_has_mutability' m: bool := match m with
| rodot | rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl_muttop | rodot_sef => true
| _ => false
end.

Notation mode_has_mutability m := ((mode_has_mutability' m) = true)(only parsing).

Inductive mode_visibility := mode_visibility_all | mode_visibility_hide_method.

Definition mode_visibility' m: mode_visibility := match m with
| rodot | rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl_muttop | rodot_sef => mode_visibility_hide_method
| _ => mode_visibility_all
end.

Notation mode_has_visibility m := ((mode_visibility' m) = mode_visibility_hide_method)(only parsing).

Inductive mode_refcaps := mode_refcaps_none | mode_refcaps_mutability.

Definition mode_refcaps' m: mode_refcaps := match m with
| rodot | rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl_muttop | rodot_sef => mode_refcaps_mutability
| _ => mode_refcaps_none
end.

Inductive mode_refcap_corr := mode_refcap_corr_same | mode_refcap_corr_ref_mutability.

Definition mode_refcap_corr' m: mode_refcap_corr := match m with
| rodot | rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl_muttop  | rodot_sef => mode_refcap_corr_ref_mutability
| _ => mode_refcap_corr_same
end.

Inductive mode_viewpoint_adaptation := mode_viewpoint_adaptation_same | mode_viewpoint_adapt_mutability.

Definition mode_viewpoint_adaptation' m: mode_viewpoint_adaptation := match m with
| rodot | rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl_muttop | rodot_sef => mode_viewpoint_adapt_mutability
| _ => mode_viewpoint_adaptation_same
end.

Inductive mode_objlit_refcaps := mode_objlit_refcaps_none | mode_objlit_refcaps_mutable.

Definition mode_objlit_refcaps' m: mode_objlit_refcaps := match m with
| rodot | rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl_muttop | rodot_sef => mode_objlit_refcaps_mutable
| _ => mode_objlit_refcaps_none
end.

Inductive mode_top_nm := mode_top_nm_none | mode_top_nm_subtype | mode_top_nm_complement.

Definition mode_top_nm' m: mode_top_nm := match m with
| rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_sef => mode_top_nm_subtype
| rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_compl_muttop  => mode_top_nm_complement
| _ => mode_top_nm_none
end.

Definition mode_has_top_nm_subtype' m: bool := match (mode_top_nm' m) with
| mode_top_nm_subtype | mode_top_nm_complement => true
| _ => false
end.

Notation mode_has_top_nm_subtype m := ((mode_has_top_nm_subtype' m) = true)(only parsing).

Notation mode_has_top_nm_complement m := ((mode_top_nm' m) = mode_top_nm_complement)(only parsing).

Notation mode_has_top_nm_subtype_boundless m := ((mode_top_nm' m) = mode_top_nm_subtype)(only parsing).

Inductive mode_mut_top := mode_mut_top_none | mode_mut_top_subtype.

Definition mode_mut_top' m: mode_mut_top := match m with
| rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl_muttop => mode_mut_top_subtype
| _ => mode_mut_top_none
end.

Notation mode_has_mut_top m := ((mode_mut_top' m) = mode_mut_top_subtype)(only parsing).

Inductive mode_incap := mode_incap_none | mode_incap_structural | mode_incap_nocap.

Definition mode_incap' m: mode_incap := match m with
| basic_incap | rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_compl_muttop | rodot_sef => mode_incap_nocap
| rodot => mode_incap_structural

Actually ty_trm_write requires x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_fld a S T) and mut_var_writeable x (x in marker bot). The mutability capability `x ∶ typ_mut_marker typ_bot` and record field a. How does that imply `x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_fld a typ_bot (marker bot))` for mreach_fld? In the mutability type system, the marker means the object is "this"-mutable, and the field's type in the object's *record* perhaps becomes dec_fld a typ_bot (marker bot) via viewpoint adaptation. mreach_fld's third premise is exactly `F ⁏ e ⊢ trm_var y1 ∶ typ_rcd (dec_fld a typ_bot (typ_mut_marker typ_bot))`. So the intended provenance requires deriving that from the writable receiver's typing.

Hmm, is that derivable? From x ∶ marker bot = typ_rcd (dec_typ refcap_mutability typ_bot typ_bot), plus x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_fld a S T) (from ty_trm_write), can we get x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_fld a typ_bot (marker bot))? Not obviously — record types with dec_fld a S T and dec_typ are different labels; no rule turns a field type into typ_bot/marker bot. Unless `typ_rcd (dec_fld a typ_bot (typ_mut_marker typ_bot))` is a *subtype* of typ_rcd (dec_fld a S T) via subtyp_fld (contravariant first, covariant second): dec_fld a S T <: dec_fld a S' T' iff S' <: S and T <: T'. So dec_fld a typ_bot (marker bot) <: dec_fld a S T iff S <: typ_bot (only if S = bot-ish) and marker bot <: T. Hmm no.

Maybe mreach_fld's typing premise is about the *declared* type of the field in the heap item's *type*, where mutability marker bot means the object is mutable, and fields of mutable objects are typed with typ_bot as their Type (for "mutable field" typing). Look at `ty_def_fld` uses dec_fld a T T (both same). Hmm. mreach_fld wants dec_fld a typ_bot (marker bot) — the Type component typ_bot and the value type marker bot. Since dec_fld's arguments are (label, Type, Value) presumably. So the field's *declared type* (upper bound) is typ_bot and the value's type is marker bot.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Require Import AbstractSyntax TypingMode GeneralTyping Indep Equivalence.

Inductive record_dec : dec -> Prop :=
| rd_typ : forall A T, record_dec (dec_typ (typ_label_normal A) T T)
| rd_typb : forall A T, record_dec (dec_typ (typ_label_normal A) typ_bot T)
| rd_fld : forall a T, record_dec (dec_fld a T T)
| rd_met : forall m TC TZ TR, record_dec (dec_met m TC TZ TR)
.

Inductive record_typ : typ -> fset label -> Prop :=
| rt_one : forall D l,
  record_dec D ->
  l = label_of D ->
  record_typ (typ_rcd D) \{l}
| rt_cons: forall T ls D l,
  record_typ T ls ->
  record_dec D ->
  l = label_of D ->
  l \notin ls ->
  record_typ (typ_and T (typ_rcd D)) (union ls \{l}).

Definition record_type T := exists ls, record_typ T ls.

Inductive refcap_dec: dec -> Prop :=
  | refcap_dec_typb lt TU:
    refcap_dec (dec_typ (typ_label_refcap lt) typ_bot TU).

Inductive refcap_typ: typ -> fset label -> Prop :=
  | refcap_typ_top:
      refcap_typ typ_top \{}
  | refcap_typ_one D l:
      refcap_dec D ->
      l = label_of D ->
      refcap_typ (typ_rcd D) \{l}
  | refcap_typ_cons T ls D l:
      refcap_typ T ls ->
      refcap_dec D ->
      l = label_of D ->
      l \notin ls ->
      refcap_typ (typ_and T (typ_rcd D)) (union ls \{l}).

Definition refcap_type T := exists ls, refcap_typ T ls.

Inductive record_has: typ -> dec -> Prop :=
| rh_one : forall D,
    record_has (typ_rcd D) D
| rh_andl : forall T U D,
    record_has T D ->
    record_has (typ_and T U) D
| rh_andr : forall T U D,
    record_has U D ->
    record_has (typ_and T U) D.

      refcap_dec D ->
      l = label_of D ->
      l \notin ls ->
      refcap_typ (typ_and T (typ_rcd D)) (union ls \{l}).

| rh_one : forall D,

| rh_andl : forall T U D,
    record_has T D ->
    record_has (typ_and T U) D
| rh_andr : forall T U D,
    record_has U D ->
    record_has (typ_and T U) D.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import Vars TransformCollect Types.

Require Import Coq.Sets.Ensembles.

Require Import Coq.Sets.Constructive_sets.

Inductive ctx: Set :=

| ctx_empty

| ctx_push: ctx -> var -> varkind -> typ -> ctx

| ctx_stop: ctx -> ctx

| ctx_hide: ctx -> ctx
.

Notation "G '§' v / vk ~ T" := (ctx_push G v vk T)
  (at level 30, vk at level 20, v at level 20, T at level 20).

Notation "v / vk ~ T" := (ctx_push ctx_empty v vk T)
  (at level 30, vk at level 20, T at level 20).

Notation "G '§ʸ' v ~ T" := (ctx_push G v v_loc T)
  (at level 30, v at level 20, T at level 20).

Notation "G '§ʷ' v ~ T" := (ctx_push G v v_ref T)
  (at level 30, v at level 20, T at level 20).

Notation "G '§ʳ' v ~ T" := (ctx_push G v v_recv T)
  (at level 30, v at level 20, T at level 20).

Notation "G '§ᶻ' v ~ T" := (ctx_push G v v_par T)
  (at level 30, v at level 20, T at level 20).

Notation "G '§ˢ' v ~ T" := (ctx_push G v v_self T)
  (at level 30, v at level 20, T at level 20).

Notation "G '§ˣ' v ~ T" := (ctx_push G v v_let T)
  (at level 30, v at level 20, T at level 20).

Fixpoint ctx_concat(G1 G2: ctx): ctx :=
match G2 with
| ctx_empty => G1
| ctx_push c v vk t => ctx_push (ctx_concat G1 c) v vk t
| ctx_stop c => ctx_stop (ctx_concat G1 c)
| ctx_hide c => ctx_hide (ctx_concat G1 c)
end.

Notation "E §& F" := (ctx_concat E F)
  (at level 28, left associativity) : env_scope.

Fixpoint ctx_map(fn: typ -> typ)(G: ctx): ctx :=
match G with
| ctx_empty => ctx_empty
| ctx_push G1 v vk t => ctx_push (ctx_map fn G1) v vk (fn t)
| ctx_stop G1 => ctx_stop (ctx_map fn G1)
| ctx_hide G1 => ctx_hide (ctx_map fn G1)
end.

Fixpoint ctx_collect_values(A: Set)(fn: typ -> fset A)(G: ctx): fset A :=
match G with
| ctx_empty => \{}
| ctx_push G1 v vk t => (fn t) \u (ctx_collect_values fn G1)
| ctx_stop G1 => (ctx_collect_values fn G1)
| ctx_hide G1 => (ctx_collect_values fn G1)
end.

Notation ctx_fv := (ctx_collect_values fv).

Instance CtxFreeVar : FreeVar ctx := ctx_fv.

Fixpoint ctx_keys(G: ctx): list var :=
match G with
| ctx_empty => nil
| ctx_push G v vk t =>  v :: (ctx_keys G)
| ctx_stop G => ctx_keys G
| ctx_hide G => ctx_keys G
end.

Fixpoint ctx_dom(G: ctx): fset var :=
match G with
| ctx_empty => \{}
| ctx_push G v vk t =>  \{ v } \u (ctx_dom G)
| ctx_stop G => ctx_dom G
| ctx_hide G => ctx_dom G
end.

Notation "x '§#' E" := (x \notin (ctx_dom E)) (at level 67) : env_scope.

Inductive ctx_ok: ctx -> Prop :=
| ctx_ok_empty:
  ctx_ok ctx_empty
| ctx_ok_push(G: ctx)(v: var)(vk: varkind)(t: typ):
  ctx_ok G ->
  v §# G ->
  ctx_ok (ctx_push G v vk t)
| ctx_ok_stop(G: ctx):
  ctx_ok G -> ctx_ok (ctx_stop G)
| ctx_ok_hide(G: ctx):
  ctx_ok G -> ctx_ok (ctx_hide G)
.

Inductive ctx_weakens: ctx -> Prop :=
| ctx_weakens_empty: ctx_weakens ctx_empty
| ctx_weakens_push G v vk t:
  ctx_weakens G ->
  ctx_weakens (ctx_push G v vk t)
.

Inductive ctx_weakens_hide: ctx -> Prop :=
| ctx_weakens_hide_empty: ctx_weakens_hide ctx_empty
| ctx_weakens_hide_push G v vk t:
    ctx_weakens_hide G ->
    ctx_weakens_hide (ctx_push G v vk t)
| ctx_weakens_hide_hide G:
    ctx_weakens_hide G ->
    ctx_weakens_hide (ctx_hide G)
.

Inductive ctx_binds: var -> typ -> ctx -> Prop :=
| ctx_binds_e(v: var)(vk: varkind)(t: typ)(G: ctx):
    ctx_binds v t (ctx_push G v vk t)
| ctx_binds_n(v v2: var)(vk: varkind)(t t2: typ)(G: ctx):
    v <> v2 ->

Great; the mutual induction recipe works and `all: try (intros; econstructor; eauto; fail)` handles most cases. For weakening the context, the analogous pattern might work with a bit of custom handling for ctx_binds/ctx_vis premises (which need to be transported via the mono hypotheses) and for pushed contexts (need the push lifting applied to the IH). Lemma imm_rules_ctx_weaken :

```
    (forall v T, ctx_binds v T G -> ctx_binds v T G') ->
    (forall v, ctx_vis G v -> ctx_vis G' v) ->
    (forall Go e t T, @ty_trm typing_mode G Go e t T -> @ty_trm typing_mode G' Go e t T) /\
    (lit) /\ (def) /\ (defs).
```

```coq
Lemma imm_ctx_binds_push_mono (G G' : ctx) (x : var) (vk : varkind) (T : typ) :
  (forall v U, ctx_binds v U G -> ctx_binds v U G') ->
```
  (forall v U, ctx_binds v U (ctx_push G x vk T) ->

  (forall v, ctx_vis (ctx_push G x vk T) v ->

(* Bindings/varkinds are monotone when pushing the same binder onto both contexts. *)
Lemma imm_ctx_binds_push_mono (G G' : ctx) (x : var) (vk : varkind) (T : typ) :
  (forall v U, ctx_binds v U G -> ctx_binds v U G') ->
  (forall v U, ctx_binds v U (ctx_push G x vk T) ->
              ctx_binds v U (ctx_push G' x vk T)).

  inversion Hb; subst.
  - apply ctx_binds_e.
  - eapply ctx_binds_n; [ eassumption | eapply Hm; eassumption ].

Lemma imm_ctx_vis_push_mono (G G' : ctx) (x : var) (vk : varkind) (T : typ) :
  (forall v, ctx_vis G v -> ctx_vis G' v) ->
  (forall v, ctx_vis (ctx_push G x vk T) v ->
            ctx_vis (ctx_push G' x vk T) v).

  intros Hm v Hv.
  inversion Hv; subst.
  - apply ctx_vis_e.
  - eapply ctx_vis_n; [ eassumption | eapply Hm; eassumption ].
Qed.

(* A record component can be projected by subtyping. *)
Lemma imm_record_has_subtyp (G : ctx) (e : renv) (T : typ) (D : dec) :
  record_has T D ->
  @subtyp typing_mode G objctx_empty e T (typ_rcd D).
Proof.

  - apply subtyp_refl.
  - eapply subtyp_trans.
    + apply subtyp_and11.
    + exact IHrecord_has.
  - eapply subtyp_trans.
    + apply subtyp_and12.
    + exact IHrecord_has.
Qed.

(* A variable whose type has a record component also has the record type. *)
Lemma imm_ty_var_record_has (G : ctx) (e : renv) (x : var) (T : typ) (D : dec) :
  @ty_var typing_mode G objctx_empty e x T ->
  record_has T D ->
  @ty_var typing_mode G objctx_empty e x (typ_rcd D).
Proof.
  intros Hx Hr.
  eapply ty_var_sub; [ exact Hx | apply imm_record_has_subtyp; exact Hr ].
Qed.

(* The object-reference type projects to the recursive record body. *)
Lemma imm_ty_var_obj_body (G : ctx) (e : renv) (x : var) (U : typ) :
  ctx_binds x (typ_objref U (typ_mut_marker typ_bot)) G ->
  typ_indep_b 0 U ->
  @ty_var typing_mode G objctx_empty e x (open x U).
Proof.
  intros Hcb Hind.
  assert (Hobj : @ty_var typing_mode G objctx_empty e x
      (typ_objref U (typ_mut_marker typ_bot)))
    by (apply ty_var_var; exact Hcb).
  assert (Hbnd : @ty_var typing_mode G objctx_empty e x (typ_bnd U)).
  { eapply ty_var_sub; [ exact Hobj | apply subtyp_and11 ]. }
  eapply ty_rec_elim; [ exact Hbnd | exact Hind ].
Qed.

(* A mutably-typed field of an object yields the canonical write-receiver type
   required by mreach_fld.  The only extra input is that the field's stored
   (declared = value) type is a subtype of the mutability marker. *)
Lemma imm_ty_var_obj_field_mut (G : ctx) (e : renv) (x : var) (U : typ)
      (a : fld_label) (S : typ) :
  ctx_binds x (typ_objref U (typ_mut_marker typ_bot)) G ->
  typ_indep_b 0 U ->
  record_has (open x U) (dec_fld a S S) ->
  @subtyp typing_mode G objctx_empty e S (typ_mut_marker typ_bot) ->
  @ty_var typing_mode G objctx_empty e x
    (typ_rcd (dec_fld a typ_bot (typ_mut_marker typ_bot))).
Proof.
  intros Hcb Hind Hrec Hsub.
  pose proof (imm_ty_var_obj_body Hcb Hind) as Hopen.
  pose proof (imm_ty_var_record_has Hopen Hrec) as Hfield.
  eapply ty_var_sub; [ exact Hfield | ].
  eapply subtyp_fld.
  - apply subtyp_bot.
  - exact Hsub.
Qed.

   record type gives field [a] the mutability-marker type, then the location
   stored in that field is mutably reachable too (this is exactly mreach_fld,
   with the receiver typing transported across the record subtyping). *)
Lemma imm_mreach_fld_of_mut_field (F : ctx) (t : trm) (fs : stack)
      (Sigma : heap) (e : renv) (Lv : fset var) (y1 y2 : var)
      (ds : defs) (a : fld_label) :

    (typ_rcd (dec_fld a (typ_mut_marker typ_bot) (typ_mut_marker typ_bot))) ->
  @mut_reach typing_mode F (t ; fs ; Sigma ; e ; Lv) y2.

  - exact Hinert.
  - exact Hmr.
  - exact Hb.
  - exact Hdf.

    + apply subtyp_bot.
    + apply subtyp_refl.
Qed.

This iteration added 8 verified lemmas completing the **static field→mutable-reachability provenance chain**:

```coq
Lemma imm_record_has_subtyp   : record_has T D -> T <: typ_rcd D.
Lemma imm_ty_var_record_has   : x : T -> record_has T D -> x : typ_rcd D.
Lemma imm_ty_var_obj_body     : ctx_binds x (typ_objref U marker) G -> typ_indep_b 0 U ->
                                x : open x U.                       (* via and11 + ty_rec_elim *)
Lemma imm_ty_var_obj_field_mut: ... record_has (open x U) (dec_fld a S S) ->
                                S <: marker -> x : typ_rcd (dec_fld a typ_bot marker).
Lemma imm_mreach_fld_of_mut_field :
  inert F -> F ⊢ C mreach y1 -> binds y1 (item_obj ds) Σ ->
  defs_has ds (def_fld a (avar_f y2)) ->
  y1 : typ_rcd (dec_fld a marker marker) -> F ⊢ C mreach y2.
Lemma imm_heap_item_obj_ty :
  initial item_obj y ⇒ ∃U, ctx_binds y (objref U marker) F ∧ typ_indep_b 0 U ∧
                       y : open y U ∧ (ds typed) ∧ defs_varkinds F ds.
Lemma imm_mreach_fld_of_heap_item : (* packages the full static mreach_fld step *)
Lemma imm_heap_item_mut_field_mreach :
  inert F -> heap_correspond F e Σ -> binds y1 (item_obj ds) Σ ->
  defs_has ds (def_fld a (avar_f y2)) -> vis_var F y1 -> F ⊢ C mreach y1 ->
```

- LANDED: `imm_ts_ctx_weaken` (ty_var/subtyp/ty_incap weakening). Proof = `ts_mutind` with motive `forall G' (mono) (vis), judgment at G'` over the three judgments, plus a purpose-built complete solver (Ltac `imm_ts_mono_binds`, `imm_ts_mono_vis`, `imm_ts_apply_ih_{var,sub,inc}`, `imm_ts_prem`, `imm_ts_case`). KEY syntactic facts discovered: (1) goals produced by applying an *inductive constructor* use the coerced/projection form `@obj_typing var (ty_var typing_mode) G ...`, `@subtyping (subtyp typing_mode) G ...`, `@obj_ref_incap (ty_incap typing_mode) G ...`, while the induction hypotheses' conclusions are stored in the raw/record-application form `@ty_var typing_mode X ...`, `@subtyp typing_mode X ...`, `@ty_incap typing_mode X ...`. Ltac match is syntactic, so the goal patterns must use the coerced form and the IH patterns the raw form. solve/refine type-checking is up to conversion, so `refine (IH G' _ _)` still works across the forms. (2) `eauto` NEVER fails — it leaves goals — so any complete solver must be wrapped as `solve [eauto N using ...]`. (3) The mono/vis hypotheses must be usable both as whole products (`exact Hm`) and under pushed contexts (`apply imm_ctx_binds_push_mono`/`imm_ctx_vis_push_mono` repeatedly). (4) `mode_visibility' typing_mode` is a variable, so `vis_hide`/`ctx_obj_met` only reduce after `rewrite imm_mode_mut_vis` (or imm_mode_vis_hide) followed by `cbn`. (5) IHs with leading variable binders (subtyp_fun/subtyp_met/lit/def_met premises like `forall x, x∉L -> forall X, mono -> vis -> J`) are applied by a generic branch `match goal with H : forall z:var, _ => eapply H; imm_prem end`, and `eapply H` unifies the evars/indices; raw-vs-coerced conversion works there.
- LANDED context-lifting helpers: `imm_ctx_binds_hide`, `imm_ctx_vis_hide` (vis of a hide context is vacuously preserved), `imm_ctx_binds_ctx_obj`, `imm_ctx_vis_ctx_obj`, `imm_ctx_binds_ctx_obj_met`, `imm_ctx_vis_ctx_obj_met` (destruct Go; `cbn [ctx_obj_met]`; `rewrite imm_mode_mut_vis`; `cbn`; then `repeat first [apply imm_ctx_binds_push_mono | apply imm_ctx_binds_hide | exact Hm]`). LANDED wrappers `imm_ts_var_weaken`, `imm_ts_sub_weaken`, `imm_ts_incap_weaken` (projections of imm_ts_ctx_weaken).
- NEXT (in progress): `imm_capbnd_ctx_weaken` via `ty_capbnd_ind` (typing_mode and C are IMPLICIT in the scheme: call `ty_capbnd_ind (fun G Go e T U => ...)`). Trivial cases by `intros; econstructor; eauto using imm_ts_var_weaken`; and/or premises solved by `refine (IH G' Hm Hv)`; the `ty_capbnd_sel` case is the only hard one because `econstructor` leaves the constructor's `S,T` as evars (they do not occur in the conclusion `typ_sel ...`). Planned fix: match the var premise `Hvar : @obj_typing var (ty_var typing_mode) G objctx_empty e x (typ_rcd (dec_typ B S T))`, the recursive IH, Hm/Hv, and rebuild with `refine (@ty_capbnd_sel typing_mode C G' e x B y S T T' _ _)` (explicit S,T from Hvar), then solve the premises with imm_ts_var_weaken/IH. `unify TG TH` DOES work on the evars, so that is not the blocker; the exact leftover after the naive refine was `ctx_binds x (typ_rcd (dec_typ B ?S ?T)) G'`, suggesting an argument-order/misalign issue in the explicit constructor application still to resolve.
- ATTEMPTED BUT NOT LANDED (superseded): full `imm_ts_ctx_weaken`

As of 2026-11-22, `/workspace/Task.v` compiles through 196 verified Lemma/Theorem declarations (including `immutability_aux`), plus 65 exported class instances. It fails only at the untouched `immutability_guarantee` target (currently line 3015; `make`: "Open proofs remain" at the End at line 3023). MAJOR MILESTONE: full type-level context weakening `imm_ts_ctx_weaken` (ty_var/subtyp/ty_incap under ctx_binds+ctx_vis monotonicity) is now proven and in Task.v, together with ctx-lifting helpers and wrappers (see below). The remaining weakening work is the term/def level (ty_trm/ty_lit/ty_def/ty_defs), plus ty_capbnd and viewpoint_adapt_cap.

Verified bricks in Task.v (grouped):
- syntax classes: FvOpenCases/FvSubstCases/SubstFresh/SubstOpenCommut for avar/typ/dec/trm/lit/def/defs/item/frame/stack/var (44 instances); generic `imm_fv_subst_subset`, `_mem`; union helpers; projection bridges; `imm_subst_open_commut_*`, `imm_subst_fresh_*`, `imm_subst_var_self/_neq`, `imm_fv_open_cases_*`, `imm_fv_subst_cases_*`.
- DerefInFv instances (4) for var/avar/def/defs (`imm_dif_*`), via `imm_fv_var`, `imm_fv_env_cons` (proved with `unfold fv_in_values; rewrite values_def`), `imm_fv_subst_mem_var/_avar`, `imm_deref_*_mem`. deref_base substitutes INSIDE the recursive call (`deref_base su ys (subst_var w y X)`) — generalize the argument in induction.
- runtime renv invariants (new): `imm_dom_env_fv_config(_mem)`, `imm_notin_dom_env_of_notin_fv_config`, `imm_fresh_one/_two`, `imm_red_renv_dom_mono`, `imm_red_closure_renv_dom_subset`, `imm_red_renv_binds_mono`, `imm_red_closure_renv_binds_mono`. Heap analogues were already present (`imm_red_dom_mono`, `imm_red_closure_dom_subset`).
- provenance: `imm_mode_mut_vis`, `imm_mode_mut_viewpoint`, `imm_ty_trm_write_typed`, `imm_write_at_start_mreach` (n=0).
- renv-extension monotonicity for all typing judgments: `imm_tyq_var/typ_renv_mono`, `imm_ts_renv_mono`, `imm_capbnd_renv_mono`, `imm_viewpoint_cap_renv_mono`, `imm_rules_renv_mono`.

Important negative finding: fv_config is NOT monotone along red. In red_let_var, `(trm_var x; frame_let u::fs)` becomes `(open x u; fs)`; if u ignores its bound variable, fv(open x u)=fv u and x can disappear from the config's free variables. So the useful runtime invariant is renv/heap domain+binds monotonicity (proved), not fv_config subset; for freshness preservation one would need the reverse containment fv_new ⊆ fv_old ∪ fresh.

Strategic observations (CORRECTED):
- WRONG earlier note: `closed a := forall n x, open_rec n x a = a` does NOT forbid bound variables. It is locally-closed (no dangling de Bruijn indices): e.g. `closed (trm_let (trm_var (avar_f x)) (trm_var (avar_b 0)))` holds because the let body's avar_b 0 is opened at depth S n, never replaced (the opening reduces to an `If S n = 0 ...` which is identity by `If_r` since `S n <> 0`). Hence `config_closed` does NOT make runtime openings identities; the operational semantics does perform real substitution via bound variables. The full substitution/renaming metatheory for typings is therefore still required.
- New `ctx_rem x G G'` relation (binder removal, topmost occurrence; push/stop/hide congruence) is in Task.v with `imm_ctx_binds_rem` and `imm_ctx_vis_rem`: `ctx_binds v T G -> ctx_rem x G G' -> v<>x -> ctx_binds v T G'`, same for ctx_vis. This is the context plumbing for a future typing-strengthening induction. Caveat: a rule's own binder z in a given derivation may equal the removed x, in which case the opened premise's term can contain x even if the top term does not; the strengthening statement must handle this (e.g. via a renamed/alpha-variant derivation or a hypothesis that x avoids all binder names used by the derivation).
- Still needed: typing strengthening/substitution mutual inductions over ts/rules/capbnd, plus provenance. None exists in the proof-stripped library.
- New small lemmas: generic `imm_fv_open_subset`/`_mem` (companions of `imm_fv_subst_subset`).
- Also added `imm_subst_ctx_push/_hide/_stop` (ctx_map only substitutes binder *types*, not binder names) and `imm_ctx_rem_dom_in` / `imm_ctx_rem_dom_subset`.
- `ctx` induction gotcha: ctx_push's recursive argument is FIRST, so its induction pattern is `[| G0 IH v vk t | G0 IH | G0 IH]` (IH before v/vk/t), not the intuitive `[| G0 v vk t IH | ...]`; the latter silently binds IH to the typ and breaks `rewrite IH`.
- Added `imm_ctx_binds_subst`, `imm_ctx_vis_subst`, `imm_ctx_dom_subst`, `imm_ctx_ok_subst`: ctx_map (subst_ctx) preserves binder lookups/visibility/domain/ok up to substituted types (binder names unchanged).
- Added `imm_ctx_k_weaken_fresh` (ctx_k preserved when pushing a binder fresh for the context) and `imm_all_tfree_k_push` (all_tfree_k preserved under a fresh binder push). Needed ingredients: `imm_binds_k_after_binds` + `@imm_ctx_binds_dom` (note: imm_ctx_binds_dom's G,x,T args are implicit, call with `@`).
- Added `imm_tfree_open_trm` (TFreeOpen for trm/lit/def/defs, proven via `tfree_mutind` with motive `fun v t d => forall n, tfree v (open_rec n x t)`; blanket `intros; cbn; econstructor; eauto` leaves the 9 recursive cases, solved by applying the IH at depth n, S n, or S(S n) per the open_rec depth) and `imm_tfree_open_stack`.
- Useful inversion recipe: the `tfree` judgment is a class projection; before inversion do `change (tfree_trm v <term>) in H` (or tfree_stack etc.) to expose the concrete inductive, then `inversion H` automatically discriminates the impossible avar_b cases. This is the key to finishing TFreeOpenInv too.
- Added `imm_avar_open_eq : open_rec k x a = avar_f v -> a = avar_f v \/ v = x` (destruct a; avar_b first!; `unfold open_rec, AvarOpenable in E; cbn in E`; If_l/If_r; injection/discriminate). This is the key avar case for TFreeOpenInv.
- COMPLETED TFreeOpenInv (`imm_tfree_open_inv_trm` mutual for trm/lit/def/defs, per-type `imm_tfree_open_inv`, `_lit`, `_def`, `_defs`, `imm_tfree_open_inv_stack`, and 5 exported TFreeOpenInv instances). Winning recipe (avoids trm_mutind naming/depth pain): prove the `TFreeOpenInvInd` form `tfree v t -> forall k x tR, t = open_rec k x tR -> tfree v tR \/ v=x` by `apply tfree_mutind`; in each constructor case `destruct tR; cbn in H; try discriminate; injection H as ...`, then use `imm_avar_open_eq` for avar positions (with `eq_sym`; in Task.v's Set-Implicit-Arguments context call it as `@imm_avar_open_eq k x v a H`). The inductive IH is at arbitrary k, so depths are handled. Then derive the class field by instantiating t := open n x t0, tR := t0, eq_refl.
- SOLVED the TFreeOpen-instance problem: define per-type wrappers `imm_tfree_open_trm1/_lit1/_def1/_defs1/_stack1` with explicit `(v x t n)` order (proved by `exact (proj1 (imm_tfree_open_trm x) v t H n)`, and the stack one by `@imm_tfree_open_stack x s v H n`), then register the 5 `TFreeOpen` instances. The wrappers defeat the implicit-argument misparse.
- Added `imm_tfree_in_fv_trm` (TFreeInFV for trm/lit/def/defs): state it with CONCRETE `fv_trm/_lit/_def/_defs`; then `apply tfree_mutind; all: try (intros; cbn; try rewrite in_union; auto using in_singleton_self; fail); all: intros; eauto using in_singleton_self` closes all 18 cases. Projection-form per-type corollaries (`imm_tfree_in_fv`, `_lit`, `_def`, `_defs`) follow by `exact (proj1 ...)` etc.; `imm_tfree_in_fv_stack` by induction on the tfree_stack derivation (cons_l uses the trm component). With this, the TFree dictionary is complete (TFreeOpen lemmas+instances, TFreeOpenInv lemmas+instances, TFreeInFV lemmas).
- COMPLETED the SubstIntro class layer (`open n y X = subst x y (open n x X)` when x ∉ fv X): avar helpers `imm_avar_subst_self/_neq/_subst_intro`; `imm_typ_subst_intro` (typ/dec mutual via typ_mutind, motive `forall n, x∉fv T -> ...`, cbn; f_equal; IHs at n/S n/S(S n); split fv with notin_union_r; typ_sel uses the avar helper; dec_met splits the 3-way fv with nested notin_union_r); `imm_trm_subst_intro` (trm/lit/def/defs mutual via trm_mutind, same style; lit_fun/lit_obj/def_typ use the typ component Htyp); `imm_frame/item/stack_subst_intro`; 7 exported SubstIntro instances. Gotchas: do NOT `cbn` before rewriting `imm_avar_subst_self/_neq` (cbn unfolds the avar subst projection and destroys the pattern); the class field order is `(x y n X)` so frame/item/stack instances need wrapper lambdas with `@lemma x y f n H`; the trm/lit/def/defs component applications `(proj1 (imm_trm_subst_intro x y)) t n H` work as-is.
- Added get_def/defs_has helpers: `imm_get_def_cons_eq` (label_of d = l -> get_def l (defs_cons ds d) = Some d), `imm_get_def_cons_neq`, `imm_defs_has_cons` (defs_has (cons ds d) d0 -> d0=d \/ defs_has ds d0). IMPORTANT: in Task.v's Set-Implicit-Arguments context the l/ds/d args of these lemmas become implicit enough that `(imm_get_def_cons_eq _ _ _ E)` mis-parses; call as `@imm_get_def_cons_eq (label_of d0) ds d E` (same for _neq).
- COMPLETED the canonical-forms lemma for defs typing (red_read provenance path): `imm_dec_typing_fld` (a `def_fld a (avar_f v)` dec typing yields `exists S, D = dec_fld a S S /\ v ∶ S` at ctx_obj G Go) and `imm_defs_typing_has_fld` (from `ty_defs G Go e ds T` + `defs_has ds (def_fld a (avar_f v))`, yields `exists S, record_has T (dec_fld a S S) /\ v ∶ S` at ctx_obj G Go). Proof: induct on ds; `inversion Hds` on the concrete `@ty_defs` gives exactly the two ty_defs_one/ty_defs_cons goals; split `defs_has` with `@imm_defs_has_cons`; head case uses `@imm_dec_typing_fld`; tail uses the IH; record_has via rh_one / rh_andr / rh_andl. Also `imm_defs_has_nil`.
- Added `imm_defs_has_varkind`: defs_varkinds G ds + defs_has ds (def_fld a (avar_f v)) -> ctx_k G v v_loc (induction on defs_varkinds; imm_defs_has_cons; invert def_varkinds) and `imm_heap_item_has_fld`: inert F -> heap_correspond F e S -> binds y (item_obj ds) S -> defs_has ds (def_fld a (avar_f v)) -> exists U S0, ctx_binds y (typ_objref U (marker bot)) F /\ record_has (open y U) (dec_fld a S0 S0) /\ v ∶ S0 at F,e (composition of imm_heap_item_typ and imm_defs_typing_has_fld; note Hds is convertible to the concrete @ty_defs form used by the latter).
- Added context push monotonicity: `imm_ctx_binds_push_mono` and `imm_ctx_vis_push_mono`: (forall v U, ctx_binds v U G -> ctx_binds v U G') -> same after pushing the SAME x/vk/T on both contexts (proof: invert the ctx_binds/ctx_vis derivation; top case rebuilt with ctx_binds_e/ctx_vis_e, tail with _n using the mono hyp). These are the bottom layer of general typing weakening.
- Added `imm_mreach_renv_heap_mono`: mreach F (t;fs;Sigma;e;Lv) y -> (binds w y e -> binds w y e') -> (binds z it Sigma -> binds z it Sigma') -> mreach F (t;fs;Sigma';e';Lv) y. Proof via `mut_reach_ind` with an explicit config-destructing motive `match C0 with config_mk t0 fs0 Sigma0 e0 Lv0 => forall Sigma' e', mono e0 e' -> mono Sigma0 Sigma' -> @mut_reach typing_mode F0 (mk t0 fs0 Sigma' e' Lv0) y0 end`. CRITICAL: the motive MUST depend on the config index; otherwise the IH is stated for the goal's Sigma'/e' and the constructor premises' Sigma0/e0 are unlinked (binds mono hyp can't apply). This iteration landed the **full type-level weakening theorem** plus its lifting infrastructure — a core piece of the missing roDOT metatheory.

```coq
Lemma imm_ts_ctx_weaken :
  (forall G Go e v T, @ty_var  typing_mode G Go e v T ->
     forall G', mono_binds G G' -> mono_vis G G' -> @ty_var  typing_mode G' Go e v T) /\
  (forall G Go e T U, @subtyp typing_mode G Go e T U ->
     forall G', mono_binds G G' -> mono_vis G G' -> @subtyp typing_mode G' Go e T U) /\
  (forall G Go e T U, @ty_incap typing_mode G Go e T U ->
     forall G', mono_binds G G' -> mono_vis G G' -> @ty_incap typing_mode G' Go e T U).
```

It is proved by a mutual induction with a purpose-built complete solver (`imm_ts_prem`/`imm_ts_case`). Key facts discovered and encoded:
- Constructor-generated goals use the coerced forms (`@obj_typing var (ty_var typing_mode)`, `@subtyping (subtyp typing_mode)`, `@obj_ref_incap (ty_incap typing_mode)`), while IH conclusions are stored in the raw form (`@ty_var typing_mode`, `@subtyp typing_mode`, `@ty_incap typing_mode`) — Ltac matching must use the respective forms.
- `eauto` never fails, so complete search needs `solve [eauto N using …]`.
- Mono/vis hypotheses are needed both as whole products (`exact Hm`) and lifted through pushes (`apply imm_ctx_binds_push_mono`).
- IHs with leading variables (`subtyp_fun`, `subtyp_met`, etc.) are discharged by `eapply H; imm_prem`.

Also added verified context-lifting helpers `imm_ctx_binds_hide`, `imm_ctx_vis_hide` (visibility through a hidden context is vacuous), `imm_ctx_binds_ctx_obj`, `imm_ctx_vis_ctx_obj`, and the `ctx_obj_met` versions (using `rewrite imm_mode_mut_vis` to reduce `vis_hide`), plus the wrappers `imm_ts_var/sub/incap_weaken`.

Progress on the remaining layers: `imm_capbnd_ctx_weaken` via `ty_capbnd_ind` is next; all cases except `ty_capbnd_sel` are closed, and the sel case's constructor leaves `S,T` as evars (they don't occur in `typ_sel ...`), so it needs an explicit-constructor application using the types from the variable premise — being debugged.

Status: **196 verified declarations + 65 instances**; `make` fails only at `immutability_guarantee` (line 3015), target byte-identical to `Task.v.orig`, no `Admitted`/`admit`/`Abort`/axioms. Remaining missing pieces: term/def-level weakening, capbnd + viewpoint weakening, binder-removal substitution/renaming, config-typing preservation, and the read/write provenance invariant.

All ~44 constructor cases are individually provable (e.g. ty_rec_intro via the IH + incap IH), but the automated multi-constructor search kept leaving pushed-context IH goals; no partial/Admitted version is in Task.v. The two push lemmas above are the verified extracted part.

Given the huge progress on weakening, maybe now attempt a *specific* substitution lemma needed for the operational semantics: the runtime opens terms with a variable (`open x t`), and we need typing preservation under opening. The standard roDOT proof needs:
- typing_rename / typing_subst / typing_strengthen.

Perhaps we can target the simplest needed piece: **typing of `open x t` from typing of `t` in an extended context plus typing of x**. This is the "open substitution" lemma for type variables (not term substitution): in DOT, `t` typed in `G § x ~ T` and x typed at T in G implies `open x t`? No—opening substitutes a *variable* for a binder; the judgment in the extended context uses the binder internally, so opening with the same variable doesn't change the term's meaning (it's the identity?).

Actually the runtime semantics uses `open x t` = open_rec 0 x t, replacing the bound variable 0 with free x. The typing rule ty_trm_let has premise `forall x, x∉L -> G § x ~ T ⊢ open x u : U` — the premise already contains the opened term. Lemma imm_ty_item_s_heap_push (G : ctx) (e : renv) (s : heap) (z : var) :

  forall (y : var) (it : item), y \notin dom s ->

CRITICAL: the motive MUST depend on the config index; otherwise the IH is stated for the goal's Sigma'/e' and the constructor premises' Sigma0/e0 are unlinked (binds mono hyp can't apply). Also: `mut_reach_ind`'s typing_mode is implicit; c/c0/v and the derivation are implicit too, so use `refine (mut_reach_ind P _ _ Hmr)` (NOT `mut_reach_ind typing_mode P`). premise binder order in the fld case is: inert, mreach premise, IH, binds, defs_has, typing.

This iteration built the **config-correspondence extension layer** needed to preserve well-typedness as the heap and context grow during reduction:

```coq
Lemma imm_renv_corr_push : renv_corr G e -> y0 §# G -> renv_corr (G § y0/vk ~ T0) e.

Lemma imm_ctx_binds_push_fresh : x §# G -> (mono G (G § x/vk ~ T)).
Lemma imm_ctx_vis_push_any   : mono_vis G (G § x/vk ~ T).
Lemma imm_ctx_binds_swap / imm_ctx_vis_swap :  (* binder commutation *)
  y §# G -> mono (G § x/vk ~ T) ((G § y/vk2 ~ T2) § x/vk ~ T).

Lemma imm_def_varkinds_push / imm_defs_varkinds_push :
  defs_varkinds G ds -> x §# G -> defs_varkinds (G § x/vk ~ T) ds.

Lemma imm_ty_item_s_push       : ty_item_s G e S z -> x §# G ->
                                 ty_item_s (G § x/vk ~ T) e S z.
Lemma imm_ty_item_s_heap_push  : ty_item_s G e s z -> y ∉ dom s ->
                                 ty_item_s G e (s & y ~ it) z.

Lemma imm_heap_correspond_push :
  heap_correspond F e S ->
  y ∉ ctx_dom F -> y ∉ dom S ->
  ty_item_s (F § y/v_loc ~ T) e (S & y ~ it) y ->
  heap_correspond (F § y/v_loc ~ T) e (S & y ~ it).
```

Notable technical points:
- `ty_item_s_push` / `ty_item_s_heap_push` are proved via `ty_item_s_ind` (its `typing_mode` and indices are implicit: `refine (ty_item_s_ind P _ _ His)`); `inversion ... as [...]` is painful here because the section-generalized `typing_mode` is the first constructor argument.
- The commutation lemmas are obtained cleanly from `imm_ctx_binds_push_mono` + `imm_ctx_binds_push_fresh` (and the vis analogue), avoiding inversion-name issues; they discharge the fun-body premise of `ty_item_s` after reordering the fresh binder.
- `heap_correspond_push` needs `If_l`/`If_r` for the `ctx_kdom` equations — `cbn` does not reduce TLC's `If (v_loc = v_loc) then …` — plus `dom_push`, `ok_push`, `ctx_ok_push`, `ctx_weakens_push`, and the old items are transported via `imm_ty_item_s_push ∘ imm_ty_item_s_heap_push`.

Status: **212 verified declarations + 65 instances**; `make` fails only at `immutability_guarantee` (line 3478), target byte-identical to `Task.v.orig`, no `Admitted`/`admit`/`Abort`/axioms.

Remaining soundness metatheory: environment extension by a *matched ref/location pair* (`renv_corr` constructor-level), stack-typing preservation, subject reduction for the active term (opening/renaming), and finally the read/write mutable-reachability provenance invariant.

Important negative finding: fv_config is NOT monotone along red. In red_let_var, `(trm_var x; frame_let u::fs)` becomes `(open x u; fs)`; if u ignores its bound variable, fv(open x u)=fv u and x can disappear from the config's free variables. So the useful runtime invariant is renv/heap domain+binds monotonicity (proved), not fv_config subset; for freshness preservation one would need the reverse containment fv_new ⊆ fv_old ∪ fresh.

Strategic observations (CORRECTED):
- WRONG earlier note: `closed a := forall n x, open_rec n x a = a` does NOT forbid bound variables. It is locally-closed (no dangling de Bruijn indices): e.g. `closed (trm_let (trm_var (avar_f x)) (trm_var (avar_b 0)))` holds because the let body's avar_b 0 is opened at depth S n, never replaced (the opening reduces to an `If S n = 0 ...` which is identity by `If_r` since `S n <> 0`). Hence `config_closed` does NOT make runtime openings identities; the operational semantics does perform real substitution via bound variables. The full substitution/renaming metatheory for typings is therefore still required.

Caveat: a rule's own binder z in a given derivation may equal the removed x, in which case the opened premise's term can contain x even if the top term does not; the strengthening statement must handle this (e.g. via a renamed/alpha-variant derivation or a hypothesis that x avoids all binder names used by the derivation).

Needed ingredients: `imm_binds_k_after_binds` + `@imm_ctx_binds_dom` (note: imm_ctx_binds_dom's G,x,T args are implicit, call with `@`).
- Added `imm_tfree_open_trm` (TFreeOpen for trm/lit/def/defs, proven via `tfree_mutind` with motive `fun v t d => forall n, tfree v (open_rec n x t)`; blanket `intros; cbn; econstructor; eauto` leaves the 9 recursive cases, solved by applying the IH at depth n, S n, or S(S n) per the open_rec depth) and `imm_tfree_open_stack`.

This is the key to finishing TFreeOpenInv too.
- Added `imm_avar_open_eq : open_rec k x a = avar_f v -> a = avar_f v \/ v = x` (destruct a; avar_b first!; `unfold open_rec, AvarOpenable in E; cbn in E`; If_l/If_r; injection/discriminate). This is the key avar case for TFreeOpenInv.

KEY syntactic facts discovered: (1) goals produced by applying an *inductive constructor* use the coerced/projection form `@obj_typing var (ty_var typing_mode) G ...`, `@subtyping (subtyp typing_mode) G ...`, `@obj_ref_incap (ty_incap typing_mode) G ...`, while the induction hypotheses' conclusions are stored in the raw/record-application form `@ty_var typing_mode X ...`, `@subtyp typing_mode X ...`, `@ty_incap typing_mode X ...`. Ltac match is syntactic, so the goal patterns must use the coerced form and the IH patterns the raw form. solve/refine type-checking is up to conversion, so `refine (IH G' _ _)` still works across the forms. (2) `eauto` NEVER fails — it leaves goals — so any complete solver must be wrapped as `solve [eauto N using ...]`. (3) The mono/vis hypotheses must be usable both as whole products (`exact Hm`) and under pushed contexts (`apply imm_ctx_binds_push_mono`/`imm_ctx_vis_push_mono` repeatedly). (4) `mode_visibility' typing_mode` is a variable, so `vis_hide`/`ctx_obj_met` only reduce after `rewrite imm_mode_mut_vis` (or imm_mode_vis_hide) followed by `cbn`. (5) IHs with leading variable binders (subtyp_fun/subtyp_met/lit/def_met premises like `forall x, x∉L -> forall X, mono -> vis -> J`) are applied by a generic branch `match goal with H : forall z:var, _ => eapply H; imm_prem end`, and `eapply H` unifies the evars/indices; raw-vs-coerced conversion works there.

- GOTCHA: stating typing judgments with the `∷`/`∷d` notations inside a Lemma under Set Implicit Arguments can leave *typeclass evars* (shelved `Typing defs`/`Typing var`), which then surface as "UNDEFINED EVARS" at Qed/Abort. Fix: state the judgments CONCRETELY as `@ty_defs typing_mode G Go e ds T`, `@ty_def typing_mode G Go e d D`, `@ty_var typing_mode G Go e v T`. The inversion then gives clean concrete goals.
- Original planned wording (now done): a canonical-forms lemma for defs typing: from `G §§ Go ⁏ e ⊢ ds ∶ T` and `defs_has ds (def_fld a (avar_f v))`, obtain `exists S, record_has T (dec_fld a S S) /\ ctx_obj G Go ⁏ e ⊢ v ∶ S`. Then the read typing (the field's declared type) can be related to the stored value's typing.
- Workflow caution: global `str.replace` on a scratch copy can silently corrupt *earlier* proofs when the target string occurs there too (e.g. the `imm_binds_in_dom Hb` line in imm_heap_loc_typ_mut). Always use a unique context or edit Task.v via the Edit tool; Task.v itself was not affected.
- KEY design fact: the substitution lemma needed is BINDER-REMOVAL substitution (`G § x~T` derivation + typing of y at T under G => typing of t[x:=y] under G). `ctx_map`/`subst_ctx` does NOT rename binders, so it cannot be the right context operation for substituting runtime arguments for method parameters. Also `ty_def_met`'s `open_met xz xc t` makes the parameters appear as *free avar_f names* in the opened body, so strengthening them away is impossible; genuine substitution is required. This closes off the strengthening-only shortcut.
Remaining gap overall: strengthening + provenance (typing substitution/weakening absent). See [[rodot-immutability-blocked]].

**Environment/heap correspondence extension (fresh reference pair):**
```coq
Lemma imm_renv_corr_extend :
  renv_corr G e -> w §# G -> typ_corr Tw Ty ->
  ctx_binds_k_after y v_loc Ty G G2 ->
  renv_corr (G § w/v_ref ~ Tw) (e & w ~ y).

Lemma imm_ty_item_s_renv_mono : ty_item_s G e S z -> env_binds_more e e' ->
                               ty_item_s G e' S z.

Lemma imm_heap_correspond_renv_push :
  heap_correspond F e S -> w §# F -> typ_corr Tw Ty ->
  ctx_binds_k_after y v_loc Ty F G2 ->
  heap_correspond (F § w/v_ref ~ Tw) (e & w ~ y) S.
```
The proof of `heap_correspond_renv_push` handles the `ctx_kdom` equations (`If_r` on `v_loc = v_ref`, `If_l` + `dom_push` for `v_ref`), shows `w ∉ dom e` from freshness, and transports all existing heap items through context + renv monotonicity.

**Typing inversion and the first reduction step:**
```coq
Lemma imm_ty_trm_var_inv : G⁏e ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T -> G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ T.

Lemma imm_ty_trm_let_inv :
  G⁏e ⊢ trm_let a b ∶ R ->
  exists L S, G⁏e ⊢ a ∶ S /\
    (forall x, x ∉ L -> (G § x/v_let ~ S)⁏e ⊢ open x b ∶ R).

Lemma imm_ty_stack_cons_inv :
  ty_stack G e T (frame_let t :: st) W ->
  exists L U, ty_stack G e U st W /\
    (forall x, x ∉ L -> (G § x/v_let ~ T)⁏e ⊢ open x t ∶ U).

Lemma imm_stack_push_let :
  ty_stack G e U st W -> G⁏e ⊢ trm_let a b ∶ U ->
  exists S, G⁏e ⊢ a ∶ S /\
            ty_stack G e S (frame_let b :: st) W.
```
`imm_stack_push_let` is exactly the typing preservation needed for the `red_let_push` step: the new active term is `a` and the new stack is the pushed frame.

Important negative finding: fv_config is NOT monotone along red. In red_let_var, `(trm_var x; frame_let u::fs)` becomes `(open x u; fs)`; if u ignores its bound variable, fv(open x u)=fv u and x can disappear from the config's free variables. So the useful runtime invariant is renv/heap domain+binds monotonicity (proved), not fv_config subset; for freshness preservation one would need the reverse containment fv_new ⊆ fv_old ∪ fresh.

- WRONG earlier note: `closed a := forall n x, open_rec n x a = a` does NOT forbid bound variables. It is locally-closed (no dangling de Bruijn indices): e.g. `closed (trm_let (trm_var (avar_f x)) (trm_var (avar_b 0)))` holds because the let body's avar_b 0 is opened at depth S n, never replaced (the opening reduces to an `If S n = 0 ...` which is identity by `If_r` since `S n <> 0`). Hence `config_closed` does NOT make runtime openings identities; the operational semantics does perform real substitution via bound variables. The full substitution/renaming metatheory for typings is therefore still required.

Caveat: a rule's own binder z in a given derivation may equal the removed x, in which case the opened premise's term can contain x even if the top term does not; the strengthening statement must handle this (e.g. via a renamed/alpha-variant derivation or a hypothesis that x avoids all binder names used by the derivation).

- LANDED: `imm_ts_ctx_weaken` (ty_var/subtyp/ty_incap weakening). Proof = `ts_mutind` with motive `forall G' (mono) (vis), judgment at G'` over the three judgments, plus a purpose-built complete solver (Ltac `imm_ts_mono_binds`, `imm_ts_mono_vis`, `imm_ts_apply_ih_{var,sub,inc}`, `imm_ts_prem`, `imm_ts_case`). KEY syntactic facts discovered: (1) goals produced by applying an *inductive constructor* use the coerced/projection form `@obj_typing var (ty_var typing_mode) G ...`, `@subtyping (subtyp typing_mode) G ...`, `@obj_ref_incap (ty_incap typing_mode) G ...`, while the induction hypotheses' conclusions are stored in the raw/record-application form `@ty_var typing_mode X ...`, `@subtyp typing_mode X ...`, `@ty_incap typing_mode X ...`. Ltac match is syntactic, so the goal patterns must use the coerced form and the IH patterns the raw form. solve/refine type-checking is up to conversion, so `refine (IH G' _ _)` still works across the forms. (2) `eauto` NEVER fails — it leaves goals — so any complete solver must be wrapped as `solve [eauto N using ...]`. (3) The mono/vis hypotheses must be usable both as whole products (`exact Hm`) and under pushed contexts (`apply imm_ctx_binds_push_mono`/`imm_ctx_vis_push_mono` repeatedly).   G⁏e ⊢ lit_fun S t ∶ R ->
```coq
  exists L U, R = typ_fun S U /\
    (forall x, x ∉ L -> (G § x/v_par ~ S)⁏e ⊢ open x t ∶ open x U).

Lemma imm_ty_lit_obj_inv :

  R = typ_objlit typing_mode S /\
  exists L, forall x, x ∉ L ->

```

Instead of trans, we can solve it by matching the IH's subtyp hyp *on its conclusion's right side*: the IH's subtyp is `subtyp U0 T0` where T0 is the sub premise's left type (the same as Hsub's left). Important negative finding: fv_config is NOT monotone along red. In red_let_var, `(trm_var x; frame_let u::fs)` becomes `(open x u; fs)`; if u ignores its bound variable, fv(open x u)=fv u and x can disappear from the config's free variables. So the useful runtime invariant is renv/heap domain+binds monotonicity (proved), not fv_config subset; for freshness preservation one would need the reverse containment fv_new ⊆ fv_old ∪ fresh.

CRITICAL: the motive MUST depend on the config index; otherwise the IH is stated for the goal's Sigma'/e' and the constructor premises' Sigma0/e0 are unlinked (binds mono hyp can't apply). Also: `mut_reach_ind`'s typing_mode is implicit; c/c0/v and the derivation are implicit too, so use `refine (mut_reach_ind P _ _ Hmr)` (NOT `mut_reach_ind typing_mode P`). premise binder order in the fld case is: inert, mreach premise, IH, binds, defs_has, typing.

Important negative finding: fv_config is NOT monotone along red. In red_let_var, `(trm_var x; frame_let u::fs)` becomes `(open x u; fs)`; if u ignores its bound variable, fv(open x u)=fv u and x can disappear from the config's free variables. So the useful runtime invariant is renv/heap domain+binds monotonicity (proved), not fv_config subset; for freshness preservation one would need the reverse containment fv_new ⊆ fv_old ∪ fresh.

Strategic observations (CORRECTED):
- WRONG earlier note: `closed a := forall n x, open_rec n x a = a` does NOT forbid bound variables. It is locally-closed (no dangling de Bruijn indices): e.g. `closed (trm_let (trm_var (avar_f x)) (trm_var (avar_b 0)))` holds because the let body's avar_b 0 is opened at depth S n, never replaced (the opening reduces to an `If S n = 0 ...` which is identity by `If_r` since `S n <> 0`). Hence `config_closed` does NOT make runtime openings identities; the operational semantics does perform real substitution via bound variables. The full substitution/renaming metatheory for typings is therefore still required.
- New `ctx_rem x G G'` relation (binder removal, topmost occurrence; push/stop/hide congruence) is in Task.v with `imm_ctx_binds_rem` and `imm_ctx_vis_rem`: `ctx_binds v T G -> ctx_rem x G G' -> v<>x -> ctx_binds v T G'`, same for ctx_vis. This is the context plumbing for a future typing-strengthening induction. Caveat: a rule's own binder z in a given derivation may equal the removed x, in which case the opened premise's term can contain x even if the top term does not; the strengthening statement must handle this (e.g. via a renamed/alpha-variant derivation or a hypothesis that x avoids all binder names used by the derivation).

- Added `imm_ctx_binds_subst`, `imm_ctx_vis_subst`, `imm_ctx_dom_subst`, `imm_ctx_ok_subst`: ctx_map (subst_ctx) preserves binder lookups/visibility/domain/ok up to substituted types (binder names unchanged).
- Added `imm_ctx_k_weaken_fresh` (ctx_k preserved when pushing a binder fresh for the context) and `imm_all_tfree_k_push` (all_tfree_k preserved under a fresh binder push). Needed ingredients: `imm_binds_k_after_binds` + `@imm_ctx_binds_dom` (note: imm_ctx_binds_dom's G,x,T args are implicit, call with `@`).
- Added `imm_tfree_open_trm` (TFreeOpen for trm/lit/def/defs, proven via `tfree_mutind` with motive `fun v t d => forall n, tfree v (open_rec n x t)`; blanket `intros; cbn; econstructor; eauto` leaves the 9 recursive cases, solved by applying the IH at depth n, S n, or S(S n) per the open_rec depth) and `imm_tfree_open_stack`.

This iteration completed the **redex typing-inversion family** — the main prerequisite for subject reduction. Added and verified:

```coq
Lemma imm_ty_trm_lit_inv :
  G⁏e ⊢ trm_lit l u ∶ R ->
  exists L T U, (G⁏e ⊢ l ∶ T) /\ (G⁏e ⊢ U <: R) /\
    (forall x, x ∉ L -> (G § x/v_let ~ T)⁏e ⊢ open x u ∶ U).

Lemma imm_ty_trm_apply_inv :
  G⁏e ⊢ trm_apply (avar_f x) (avar_f z) ∶ R ->
  exists S T, (G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_fun S T) /\ (G⁏e ⊢ z ∶ S) /\ (G⁏e ⊢ open z T <: R).

Lemma imm_ty_trm_call_inv :
  G⁏e ⊢ trm_call (avar_f x) m (avar_f y) ∶ R ->
  exists TC TZ TR, (G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_met m TC TZ TR)) /\
    (G⁏e ⊢ y ∶ TZ) /\ (G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ open y TC) /\ (G⁏e ⊢ open_met y x TR <: R).

Lemma imm_ty_trm_read_inv :
  G⁏e ⊢ trm_read (avar_f x) a ∶ R ->
  exists S Tf U, (G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_fld a S Tf)) /\
    viewpoint_adapt typing_mode x G objctx_empty e Tf U /\ (G⁏e ⊢ U <: R).

Lemma imm_ty_trm_write_inv :
  G⁏e ⊢ trm_write (avar_f x) a (avar_f y) ∶ R ->
  exists S Tf, (G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_fld a S Tf)) /\
    (G⁏e ⊢ y ∶ S) /\ (G⁏e ⊢ Tf <: R).
```

The key to making them all go through was a uniform recipe (now recorded):
1. State the lemma with judgment **notations** so goal and IH components share the coerced/projection form.
2. `remember`/`induction`/`discriminate`, then `injection` the constructor equality.
3. In the `ty_trm_sub` case, peel **both** the nested existentials **and the conjunctions**: `repeat match goal with Hs : exists _, _ |- _ => destruct Hs | Hs : (_ /\ _) |- _ => destruct Hs end`. (Peeling only existentials was the long-standing bug — nothing then matches.)
4. `eexists …; split; eassumption` assigns all existential evars.
5. Compose the subtyping through `match goal with H2 : (G⁏e ⊢ ?U0 <: ?T0) |- _ => eapply subtyp_trans with (S := U0) (T := T0); [exact H2 | eassumption] end`.

Status: **226 verified declarations + 65 instances**; `make` fails only at `immutability_guarantee` (line 3891), target byte-identical to `Task.v.orig`, no `Admitted`/`admit`/`Abort`/axioms.

Remaining soundness metatheory: the alpha-renaming/binder-removal substitution needed to open method/function bodies at runtime variables, heap-update typing preservation (linking the written value's type to the field type), and the mutable-reachability provenance invariant.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import AbstractSyntax.

Class TypingEquiv (A : Set) := typing_equiv : renv -> A -> A -> Prop.

Notation "e ⊢ a '≈' b" := (typing_equiv e a b) (at level 40, a at level 59).

Inductive tyq_var: TypingEquiv var :=
| tyq_var_refl(e: renv)(v: var):
  typing_equiv e v v
| tyq_var_binds(e: renv)(v1 v2: var):
  renv_binds v1 v2 e ->
  typing_equiv e v1 v2
| tyq_var_sym(e: renv)(v1 v2: var):
  typing_equiv e v1 v2 ->
  typing_equiv e v2 v1
| tyq_var_trans(e: renv)(v1 v2 v3: var):
  typing_equiv e v1 v2 ->
  typing_equiv e v2 v3 ->
  typing_equiv e v1 v3
.

Existing Instance tyq_var.

Inductive tyq_typ: TypingEquiv typ :=
| tyq_typ_nulary(e: renv) T:
  typ_nulary T ->
    typing_equiv e T T
| tyq_typ_andor T (e: renv) t11 t12 t21 t22:
  typ_andor T ->
    typing_equiv e t11 t21 ->
    typing_equiv e t12 t22 ->
    typing_equiv e (T t11 t12) (T t21 t22)
| tyq_typ_fun (e: renv) t11 t12 t21 t22:
    typing_equiv e t11 t21 ->
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t12) (open x t22)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_fun t11 t12) (typ_fun t21 t22)
| tyq_typ_fld (e: renv) a t11 t12 t21 t22:
    typing_equiv e t11 t21 ->
    typing_equiv e t12 t22 ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_rcd (dec_fld a t11 t12)) (typ_rcd (dec_fld a t21 t22))
| tyq_typ_typ (e: renv) B t11 t12 t21 t22:
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t11) (open x t21)) ->
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t12) (open x t22)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_rcd (dec_typ B t11 t12)) (typ_rcd (dec_typ B t21 t22))
| tyq_typ_sel_normal(e: renv)(v1 v2: var) (v3: avar)(l: typ_normal_label):
    typing_equiv e v1 v2 ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_sel (avar_f v1) (typ_label_normal l) v3) (typ_sel (avar_f v2) (typ_label_normal l) v3)
| tyq_typ_sel(e: renv)(v1 v2: avar)(l: typ_label):
    typing_equiv e (typ_sel v1 l v2) (typ_sel v1 l v2)
| tyq_typ_bnd(e: renv)(t1 t2: typ):
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t1) (open x t2)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_bnd t1) (typ_bnd t2)
| tyq_typ_met m (e: renv) t11 t12 t13 t21 t22 t23:
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t11) (open x t21)) ->
    typing_equiv e t12 t22 ->
    (forall x y, typing_equiv e (open_met x y t13) (open_met x y t23)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_rcd (dec_met m t11 t12 t13)) (typ_rcd (dec_met m t21 t22 t23))
.

Existing Instance tyq_typ.

Inductive tyq_var_alt: renv -> var -> var -> Prop :=
| tyq_var_alt_eq e v:
    tyq_var_alt e v v
| tyq_var_alt_wy e w y:
    binds w y e ->
    tyq_var_alt e w y
| tyq_var_alt_yw e w y:
    binds w y e ->
    tyq_var_alt e y w
| tyq_var_alt_ww e w1 w2 y:

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import AbstractSyntax Context Defs Heap.

Class TFree(A : Set) := tfree: var -> A -> Prop.

Inductive tfree_trm: TFree trm :=

| tfree_trm_var v:
  tfree_trm v (trm_var (avar_f v))

| tfree_trm_read v1 l:
  tfree_trm v1 (trm_read (avar_f v1) l)

| tfree_trm_apply_l v1 a2:
  tfree_trm v1 (trm_apply (avar_f v1) a2)
| tfree_trm_apply_r a1 v2:
  tfree_trm v2 (trm_apply a1 (avar_f v2))

| tfree_trm_let_l v t1 t2:
  tfree_trm v t1 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_let t1 t2)
| tfree_trm_let_r v t1 t2:
  tfree_trm v t2 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_let t1 t2)

| tfree_trm_lit_l v t1 t2:
  tfree_lit v t1 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_lit t1 t2)
| tfree_trm_lit_r v t1 t2:
  tfree_trm v t2 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_lit t1 t2)

| tfree_trm_write_l v1 a2 l:
  tfree_trm v1 (trm_write (avar_f v1) l a2)
| tfree_trm_write_r a1 v2 l:
  tfree_trm v2 (trm_write a1 l (avar_f v2))

| tfree_trm_call_l v1 a2 l:
  tfree_trm v1 (trm_call (avar_f v1) l a2)
| tfree_trm_call_r a1 v2 l:
  tfree_trm v2 (trm_call a1 l (avar_f v2))

with tfree_lit: TFree lit :=

| tfree_lit_fun v t T:
  tfree_trm v t ->
  tfree_lit v (lit_fun T t)
| tfree_lit_obj v t T:
  tfree_defs v t ->
  tfree_lit v (lit_obj T t)

with tfree_def: TFree def :=

| tfree_def_trm v l:
  tfree_def v (def_fld l (avar_f v))

| tfree_def_met v t l:
  tfree_trm v t ->
  tfree_def v (def_met l t)

with tfree_defs: TFree defs :=

| tfree_defs_cons_l v d ds:
  tfree_defs v ds ->
  tfree_defs v (defs_cons ds d)
| tfree_defs_cons_r v d ds:
  tfree_def v d ->
  tfree_defs v (defs_cons ds d)
.

Scheme tfree_trm_mut    := Induction for tfree_trm Sort Prop
with   tfree_lit_mut    := Induction for tfree_lit Sort Prop
with   tfree_def_mut    := Induction for tfree_def Sort Prop
with   tfree_defs_mut   := Induction for tfree_defs Sort Prop.

Combined Scheme tfree_mutind from tfree_trm_mut, tfree_lit_mut,
tfree_def_mut, tfree_defs_mut.

Inductive tfree_stack: TFree stack :=

| tfree_stack_cons_l v t st:
  tfree_trm v t ->
  tfree_stack v (stack_cons (frame_let t) st)
| tfree_stack_cons_r v f st:
  tfree_stack v st ->
  tfree_stack v (stack_cons f st)
.

Existing Instance tfree_trm.

Existing Instance tfree_lit.

Existing Instance tfree_def.

Existing Instance tfree_defs.

Existing Instance tfree_stack.

Definition all_tfree_k {A: Set} {AT: TFree A} G (t:A) vk :=
  forall v, tfree v t -> ctx_k G v vk.

Notation all_tfree_k_trm := (@all_tfree_k trm _).

```coq
  mono_binds G G' -> mono_vis G G' -> ty_stack G' e T s U.
```

Important negative finding: fv_config is NOT monotone along red. In red_let_var, `(trm_var x; frame_let u::fs)` becomes `(open x u; fs)`; if u ignores its bound variable, fv(open x u)=fv u and x can disappear from the config's free variables. So the useful runtime invariant is renv/heap domain+binds monotonicity (proved), not fv_config subset; for freshness preservation one would need the reverse containment fv_new ⊆ fv_old ∪ fresh.

Strategic observations (CORRECTED):
- WRONG earlier note: `closed a := forall n x, open_rec n x a = a` does NOT forbid bound variables. It is locally-closed (no dangling de Bruijn indices): e.g. `closed (trm_let (trm_var (avar_f x)) (trm_var (avar_b 0)))` holds because the let body's avar_b 0 is opened at depth S n, never replaced (the opening reduces to an `If S n = 0 ...` which is identity by `If_r` since `S n <> 0`). Hence `config_closed` does NOT make runtime openings identities; the operational semantics does perform real substitution via bound variables. The full substitution/renaming metatheory for typings is therefore still required.

Caveat: a rule's own binder z in a given derivation may equal the removed x, in which case the opened premise's term can contain x even if the top term does not; the strengthening statement must handle this (e.g. via a renamed/alpha-variant derivation or a hypothesis that x avoids all binder names used by the derivation).

```coq
Lemma imm_ty_stack_ctx_weaken : ty_stack G e T s U ->
  mono_binds G G' -> mono_vis G G' -> ty_stack G' e T s U.

Lemma imm_tyq_var_subst (z x : var) (e : renv) :
  z ∉ dom e -> z ∉ fv_env e ->
  forall v1 v2 : var, e ⊢ v1 ≈ v2 -> e ⊢ subst_var z x v1 ≈ subst_var z x v2.
```

The `sym`/`trans` cases use the induction hypotheses, which regain the context-dependent freshness hypotheses because `induction` generalizes `e`; the robust application is `first [ exact IH | exact (IH Hd Hf) ]`.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses AbstractSyntax.

Require Import Vars Types Context Env Equivalence.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Inductive typ_indep: avar -> typ -> Prop :=
| typ_indep_nulary v T:
  typ_nulary T -> typ_indep v T

| typ_indep_and v t1 t2:
    typ_indep v t1->
    typ_indep v t2->
    typ_indep v (typ_and t1 t2)
| typ_indep_or v t1 t2:
    typ_indep v t1->
    typ_indep v t2->
    typ_indep v (typ_or t1 t2)
| typ_indep_fld v a t1 t2:
    typ_indep v t1->
    typ_indep v t2->
    typ_indep v (typ_rcd (dec_fld a t1 t2))
| typ_indep_typ_f v a t1 t2:
    typ_indep (avar_f v) t1->
    typ_indep (avar_f v) t2->
    typ_indep (avar_f v) (typ_rcd (dec_typ a t1 t2))
| typ_indep_typ_b n a t1 t2:
    typ_indep (avar_b (S n)) t1->
    typ_indep (avar_b (S n)) t2->
    typ_indep (avar_b n) (typ_rcd (dec_typ a t1 t2))
| typ_indep_fun_f v t1 t2:
    typ_indep (avar_f v) t1 ->
    typ_indep (avar_f v) t2 ->
    typ_indep (avar_f v) (typ_fun t1 t2)
| typ_indep_fun_b n t1 t2:
    typ_indep (avar_b n) t1 ->
    typ_indep (avar_b (S n)) t2 ->
    typ_indep (avar_b n) (typ_fun t1 t2)
| typ_indep_sel(v v1 v2: avar)(l: typ_label):
    v <> v1 ->
    v <> v2 ->
    typ_indep v (typ_sel v1 l v2)
| typ_indep_sel_normal(v v1 v2: avar)(l: typ_normal_label):
    v <> v2 ->
    typ_indep v (typ_sel v1 (typ_label_normal l) v2)
| typ_indep_bnd_f v t:

Instance TypOpenable : Openable typ := open_rec_typ.

Instance DecOpenable : Openable dec := open_rec_dec.

Fixpoint fv_typ (T: typ) : vars :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => \{}
  | typ_bot        => \{}
  | typ_rcd D      => (fv_dec D)
  | typ_and T U    => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | typ_or T U    => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | typ_sel x L y   => (fv x) \u (fv y)
  | typ_bnd T      => (fv_typ T)
  | typ_fun T1 T2  => (fv_typ T1) \u (fv_typ T2)
  | typ_nocap => \{}
  end with
fv_dec (D: dec) : vars :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | dec_fld m T U => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | dec_met m TC TZ TR => (fv_typ TC) \u (fv_typ TZ) \u (fv_typ TR)
  end.

Instance TypFreeVar : FreeVar typ := fv_typ.

Instance DecFreeVar : FreeVar dec := fv_dec.

Fixpoint subst_typ (z: var) (u: var) (T: typ) { struct T } : typ :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => typ_top
  | typ_bot        => typ_bot
  | typ_rcd D      => typ_rcd (subst_dec z u D)
  | typ_and T1 T2  => typ_and (subst_typ z u T1) (subst_typ z u T2)
  | typ_or T1 T2  => typ_or (subst_typ z u T1) (subst_typ z u T2)
  | typ_sel x L y    => typ_sel (subst_var z u x) L (subst_var z u y)
  | typ_bnd T      => typ_bnd (subst_typ z u T)
  | typ_fun T U    => typ_fun (subst_typ z u T) (subst_typ z u U)
  | typ_nocap => typ_nocap
  end with
subst_dec (z: var) (u: var) (D: dec) { struct D } : dec :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => dec_typ L (subst_typ z u T) (subst_typ z u U)
  | dec_fld L T U => dec_fld L (subst_typ z u T) (subst_typ z u U)
  | dec_met m TC TZ TR => dec_met m (subst_typ z u TC) (subst_typ z u TZ) (subst_typ z u TR)
  end.

Instance TypSubstVar : SubstVar typ := subst_typ.

Instance DecSubstVar : SubstVar dec := subst_dec.

content.content:
Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import AbstractSyntax.

Class TypingEquiv (A : Set) := typing_equiv : renv -> A -> A -> Prop.

Notation "e ⊢ a '≈' b" := (typing_equiv e a b) (at level 40, a at level 59).

Inductive tyq_var: TypingEquiv var :=
| tyq_var_refl(e: renv)(v: var):
  typing_equiv e v v
| tyq_var_binds(e: renv)(v1 v2: var):
  renv_binds v1 v2 e ->
  typing_equiv e v1 v2
| tyq_var_sym(e: renv)(v1 v2: var):
  typing_equiv e v1 v2 ->
  typing_equiv e v2 v1
| tyq_var_trans(e: renv)(v1 v2 v3: var):
  typing_equiv e v1 v2 ->
  typing_equiv e v2 v3 ->
  typing_equiv e v1 v3
.

Existing Instance tyq_var.

Inductive tyq_typ: TypingEquiv typ :=
| tyq_typ_nulary(e: renv) T:
  typ_nulary T ->
    typing_equiv e T T
| tyq_typ_andor T (e: renv) t11 t12 t21 t22:
  typ_andor T ->
    typing_equiv e t11 t21 ->
    typing_equiv e t12 t22 ->
    typing_equiv e (T t11 t12) (T t21 t22)
| tyq_typ_fun (e: renv) t11 t12 t21 t22:
    typing_equiv e t11 t21 ->
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t12) (open x t22)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_fun t11 t12) (typ_fun t21 t22)
| tyq_typ_fld (e: renv) a t11 t12 t21 t22:
    typing_equiv e t11 t21 ->
    typing_equiv e t12 t22 ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_rcd (dec_fld a t11 t12)) (typ_rcd (dec_fld a t21 t22))
| tyq_typ_typ (e: renv) B t11 t12 t21 t22:
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t11) (open x t21)) ->
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t12) (open x t22)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_rcd (dec_typ B t11 t12)) (typ_rcd (dec_typ B t21 t22))
| tyq_typ_sel_normal(e: renv)(v1 v2: var) (v3: avar)(l: typ_normal_label):
    typing_equiv e v1 v2 ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_sel (avar_f v1) (typ_label_normal l) v3) (typ_sel (avar_f v2) (typ_label_normal l) v3)
| tyq_typ_sel(e: renv)(v1 v2: avar)(l: typ_label):
    typing_equiv e (typ_sel v1 l v2) (typ_sel v1 l v2)
| tyq_typ_bnd(e: renv)(t1 t2: typ):
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t1) (open x t2)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_bnd t1) (typ_bnd t2)
| tyq_typ_met m (e: renv) t11 t12 t13 t21 t22 t23:
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t11) (open x t21)) ->
    typing_equiv e t12 t22 ->
    (forall x y, typing_equiv e (open_met x y t13) (open_met x y t23)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_rcd (dec_met m t11 t12 t13)) (typ_rcd (dec_met m t21 t22 t23))
.

Existing Instance tyq_typ.

Inductive tyq_var_alt: renv -> var -> var -> Prop :=
| tyq_var_alt_eq e v:
    tyq_var_alt e v v
| tyq_var_alt_wy e w y:

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import AbstractSyntax TypingMode GeneralTyping EnvCorrespondence Visibility TFree ConfigVarkinds Deref HeapInstantiate Indep RecordTypes InertContext RecordDefs Equivalence ConfigNotations.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

Inductive ty_item_s : ctx -> renv -> heap -> var -> Prop :=

| ty_item_fun_s : forall G e s x S t L T,
    mode_has_fun typing_mode ->
    ctx_binds x (typ_fun S T) G ->
    binds x (item_fun t) s ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G § x / v_par ~ S ⁏e ⊢ open x t ∶ open x T) ->
    all_tfree_k G t v_ref ->
    ty_item_s G e s x
| ty_item_obj_s : forall G e s x U S ds T,
    ctx_binds x T G ->
    binds x (item_obj ds) s ->
    T = typ_objref U S ->
    G §§ (objctx_heap x U) ⁏e ⊢ ds ∶ (open x U) ->
    defs_varkinds G ds ->
    ty_item_s G e s x.

Definition heap_correspond (G : ctx) (e: renv) (s : heap) : Prop :=
  ctx_ok G /\
  ctx_weakens G /\
  ok s /\
  ok e /\
  ctx_kdom v_loc G = dom s /\
  ctx_kdom v_ref G = dom e /\
  renv_corr G e /\
  (forall x,
      x \in dom s ->
      ty_item_s G e s x).

End WithTypingMode.

Arguments heap_correspond {typing_mode}.

Notation inert_G_for_item G w y T := (G § y / v_loc ~ T § w / v_ref ~ T).

Notation inert_G_for_obj G w y T S := (inert_G_for_item G w y (typ_objref T S)).

Notation heap_prefix S1 S2 := (exists S1', S2 = concat S1 S1').

  tfree_trm v2 (trm_apply a1 (avar_f v2))

  tfree_trm v t1 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_let t1 t2)

  tfree_trm v t2 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_let t1 t2)

  tfree_lit v t1 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_lit t1 t2)

  tfree_trm v t2 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_lit t1 t2)

  tfree_trm v2 (trm_write a1 l (avar_f v2))
